texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Islamuddin suffered grievous injury and sustained fracture in his left pelvis. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 03.01.2016, petitioner was travelling from Bijnaur to Delhi in car bearing no.DL-9CM-9274 alongwith other persons. The car was being driven by one Gulfam, at a normal speed on the correct side of the road. At about 11 am, when the car reached near Pulia/Bridge of Samaspur, PS Behasuma, Meerut, U.P., another car bearing no.DL-8CJ-6938 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came driven in a rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and dashed into the car in which petitioner was travelling. Due to the accident, petitioner sustained injuries and was rushed to Mawana hospital from where he was referred to Govt. hospital, Meerut and thereafter to JPN Apex Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.005/2016, dated 13.01.2016 was registered u/s 279/337/338/427 of IPC at PS Behsuma, Distt-Meerut, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. Respondent no.1 is the driver-cum-owner and respondent no.2 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Respondent no.1 filed his reply denying involvement of the vehicle in the accident and negligence on his part. He stated that his vehicle was duly insured/Respondent no.2 from 02.01.2016 to 01.01.2017 vide policy no. 2002053115P111893469. In its reply, respondent no.2 has refuted the occurrence of accident and alleged non-joinder of necessary party i.e. driver and owner of vehicle no.DL-9CM-9274. It is further pleaded that the accident appears to have occurred due to negligence of vehicle no.DL-9CM-9274 and therefore compensation, if any, is liable to be deducted. 6. Vide order dated 30.11.2019, following issues were framed. OPP 2. OPP. 3. Despite opportunity, petitioner did not lead any evidence. No evidence was either led by the respondents. Vide order dated 30.11.2019, the interest of the petitioner was also directed to be closed from such date till completion of their evidence, unless advance copy of the affidavit with documents and list of Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.19 17:26:50 +0530 MACT NO:1019/18 Islamuddin v. Md. ASif P.No. 3 Of 18 BK witnesses was supplied to the respondents. Since the order was not complied and the petitioner neither filed any list of witnesses nor supplied advance copy of his evidence, the interest of the petitioner is deemed closed with effect from 30.11.2019. The petitioner shall thus not be entitled to interest from 30.11.2019. 8.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 11. 14. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 15.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 15.7. 24. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.08.19 Date: 17:28:04 +0530 MACT NO:1019/18 Islamuddin v. Md. ASif P.No. 14 Of 18 BK beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
